Markup check: 106 of 107 raw prices land on .00/.25/.50/.75/.95/.99 with no division by 1.04-1.25 improving that -- no fee detected. Combinations items carry a menu-numbering prefix (e.g. "7. name: Gualberto's Taco Shop #2
notes: First-party site (gualbertos2.com, an OCOMNI-platform Next.js site) confirmed as the correct branch (5447 Kearny Villa Rd) but its /menu page server-renders 221 item names with the price field genuinely empty on every single one -- ordering is entirely outsourced to a Google food-ordering redirect, not usable for prices. UberEats/Postmates (Uber-owned, same company) are pure client-side SPA shells that returned nothing to curl or r.jina.ai. DoorDash does not have a listing for this branch specifically (only #1, #4 and the Imperial Ave location, which are different branches and were not used). Grubhub is a different owner and its restaurant page for this exact address (JSON-LD address confirmed 5447 Kearny Villa Rd, San Diego, CA 92123) IS server-rendered with real menu-item prices when fetched with a Googlebot user agent (a plain desktop UA hit a cookie-consent wall with no menu data; Googlebot UA bypassed it). Captured 222 items across 21 sections: Chips & Fries, Burritos, Special Burritos, Breakfast Burritos, Breakfast, Combinations, Tacos, Drinks, Super Quesadillas, Extras, Side Orders, Seafood, Enchiladas, Soups, Salads, Chimichangas, Tortas, Hamburgers, Weekly Specials, Regular Quesadillas, Tostadas & Taco Salads. Dropped the Best Sellers carousel (not diffed item by item for uniques -- given the section list above already covers every named category on the site, i.e. Chips & Fries/Burritos/etc., any Best Sellers item is necessarily a duplicate of one already in a real section). Markup check: prices land 100% on .00/.50/.99 with no division producing a cleaner distribution than the raw data -- no fee detected. Three items (Taco Salad Flying Saucer, Supreme Tostadas, Regular Tostada) showed a starting price with a trailing + (e.g. $15.50+ for size/protein choices); recorded as the base price with the + stripped.

Linked from the site is the restaurant's own Applova ordering storefront (raulsshack.applova.menu), whose address in its own JSON-LD (490 SOUTH COAST HIGHWAY, ENCINITAS, CA 92024) confirms the same branch. Its <script id=menu-structured-data> carries one complete priced Menu ("Raul's Shack - Menu"): 34 items across 8 sections (Mexican Breakfast, Breakfast Burritos, Burritos, Roll Tacos/Taquitos, Roll Tacos Burritos, Street Tacos, Fish/Shrimp/Veggie Soft Tacos, Crispy Tacos) -- this is the entire ordering menu, not a sample (only one Menu node exists in the payload). notes: Franchise first-party site pelicanausa.com is the national Wix site; its /menu page has no priced items server-rendered anywhere (checked with tag-stripped text search, no $ figures at all) and its franchisee ordering subdomain (pelicanasdconvoy.menu11.com) returns a bare "NO SITE FOUND" on every path tried, both https and http -- that platform is down/misconfigured, not just JS-gated. Used UberEats (address confirmed exact: 7767 Balboa Avenue, San Diego, CA 92111 in its own schema.org JSON-LD, read via r.jina.ai since raw curl 403s) as the primary source: 72 items across 6 real sections (Premium Chicken, Premium Boneless Chicken, Premium Fried Wings, Side Menu, Extra, Drinks) plus a Featured-items carousel dropped as duplicate. Dropped 4 further rows (Napkin, Chopstick, Spoon, Fork) priced $0.00 -- free utensils, not menu items. Cross-checked against DoorDash (address also confirmed: 7767 Balboa Avenue): of ~14 items present on both, 13 matched to the exact cent (e.g. 9pcs Crispy Fried Wings with Sauce $21.77, Peli Cheese Ball $10.98, Chicken Gangjung $26.89) and one differed slightly (HALF SAUCE-Crispy Fried Chicken: $22.82 on UberEats vs $22.99 on DoorDash -- kept UberEats' figure since UberEats is the more complete/primary source here). Flagging explicitly: raw prices do NOT cluster on .00/.25/.50/.75/.95/.99 -- cents are scattered across values like .24/.29/.38/.54/.69/.82/.86/.89/.94/.96/.98, and no single divisor (tried 1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25/0.96) cleans this up either, so it does not read as a simple percentage markup. Since two independently-owned platforms (Uber and DoorDash) show the same odd prices on nearly every item, this looks like the restaurant's actual (unusually granular) menu-11/POS pricing rather than a single-platform fee, but the pattern itself is atypical enough to hold at medium rather than high confidence.
